note_tweet.text:
[Spoiler for chapter 17]

Also, regarding Hierda and Anatoly.

I have a suspicion that the reason why Anatoly was suddenly dead due to Oripathy is simply because Hierda doesn't want to help him anymore.

The suspicion was followed from my general theory about Hierda relationship with the mutated infected, which something about Hierda's perception major influence on the mutated infected behaviour.

My reason for this assumption is because the suspicious behaviour of his death. Specifically, after Anatoly killed her mother, his Oripathy suddenly got worsen out of nowhere. And other mutated infected from Hierda's power seems doesn't follow similar behaviour. At least from what shown until now.

Following the the assumption, the other reasons is, the somehow aligned events following her character development. To be more specific, Hierda's firmed resolution that's related with her encounter with Amiya.

At one point of their encounter, Hierda seemingly got really motivated by Amiya's words, hence it gave her a firm resolve.

"Helping those who are suffer, defeating the one who inflicting suffering... that's what we should be doing."

Those Amiya wordings might got taken literally by Hierda, because it actually follows the actions and events that related to her.

The premise of Hierda mind at the time is to stop the first army cruelty led by Anatoly's mother  that caused harm for people and helping the 'suffered' Anatoly.

Furthermore, Hierda acknowledged that Anatoly is helpless, thus by letting Anatoly kill his own mother and letting him die right after may explain Hierda's perception of why she considered Anatoly's actions and her acceptance of his demise as both 'atonement' and 'salvation' correspondingly.

Then with this interpretation, we can see how literal Hierda's actions to interpret Amiya's words, by "Helping those who are suffer, defeating the one who inflicting suffering".

Perhaps for her, it's a kind of 'resolution' for the 'greater good'. Hierda's encounter with Amiya literally gave her a resolution and resolution for her own goals, which is to "ease people suffering" through her own ways.

Additionally, we can circle back to the assumption : Why Anatoly is the only shown case (so far) of the mutated infected from Hierda's direct power that died from Oripathy in such manner. (Practically not the first dying mutated infected case, because Chloe, the first identified mutated infected has also died, but she isn't 'blessed' by Hierda's power, so perhaps the new Oripathy mechanism can works differently. Especially when it's related to Hierda's power, which works upon his will consciously or unconsciouly. That's why I keep this assumption open)

———

It's really interesting to see the contrast of Hierda and Amiya, because both are actually really similar in some ways, yet circumstances says otherwise. Both are compassionate, and willing to help people with their altruistic behaviour. And funnily both are 'leaders' on their own ways. They almost like a mirror of each other in fundamental way.

But, what I think truly diverges them is the situations rhat surrounds them. Despite effectively acting as a leader for their corresponding people, Amiya practically have so many people around her to guide, comfort, protect, and walk beside her. Compared to Hierda, who effectively become the sole anchor for her people, while no one actually guides or mentally help her in equal position manner. 

While both bear the burden of leaders, both have relatively different positions from the people that surrounds them. Amiya practically have a family around her, while Hierda acts like a saviour for people around her. They effectively have different kind of mental burdens.

Furthermore, Hierda herself seemingly doesn't know the full scope of her power and its consequences, despite her genuine compassion.

note_tweet.text:
[CN SPOILER]
A small theory

I kinda suspect that the "mutated infected" hallucination is kinda affected by Hierda's perception in some ways.

Chloe (the first confirmed mutated infected) literally described the exact phenomenon that Hierda experienced after being salvaged by Priestess. 

To be more specific, Chole described her vague dreams similarly as ther phenomenons that Hierda saw when she witnessed supernova with The Presence and visit the tomb of civilization with Priestess.

Tho, this "shared vision" between the mutated infected might not exactly project Hierda's direct perception.

This assumption came from the explanation of CN anniversary's lore teaser video, where the mutated infected share similar experience of witnessing AU. And the TL said they are "seeking solace in the illusion of afterlife". (CMIIW I can't confirm the TL wordings validity)

While the AU itself is clearly a literal metaphysical space inside the Originium, the "solace" that it described may parallel with Hierda's will to seek "eternal place without sorrow". Which it is not something that Priestess aimed or at least described for, as she explicitly framed it as an expectation of ancient mythology of future that she's not buying into.

Chapter 17 also directly showed that one of the mutated infected (Anatoly) from Hierda's "blessing" saw AU directly, while she herself had never seen it on her own.

Originium might project AU as the "eternal place without sorrow" that Hierda wished.
